candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes a revision to the facility temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L to 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the operative enforceable limit is the prior 497 mg/L value, the proposed 449 mg/L value, or an unresolved revision affects which TDS limit is compared against reported measurements and whether exceedances are identified.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed TDS permit limit, in accordance with 40 CFR §133.101(f), was based 95th percentile of the most recent three years (i.e., 2018-2020) of City's wastewater treatment plant effluent net TDS data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this 95th-percentile methodology and 2018–2020 dataset define the applicable numeric limit (versus a different basis or period) could change the enforceable TDS limit used in compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The 30-day average mass loading limit is, also, revised to 24,992lbs/day from 27,664 lbs/day based on the proposed 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of whether the mass-loading limit (24,992 lbs/day vs. 27,664 lbs/day) is operative, and how it ties to the TDS concentration limit, could change which numeric limit applies to mass-based TDS measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The facility is required to continue maintaining the formulated BMP activities and monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis with reporting results monthly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this establishes a continuing monthly effluent monitoring and reporting obligation for FY2025 affects which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable (B) and how missing or non-numeric results are classified when expected monthly evidence is absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: if a discharge poses the reasonable potential to cause an in-stream excursion above a water quality criterion, the permit must contain an effluent limit for that pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reasonable-potential findings trigger mandatory effluent limits and associated monitoring for specific pollutants affects which numeric limits are treated as enforceable (A) and which pollutant-specific monitoring obligations follow from RP determinations (B).

candidates.exact_span: The facility is designated a major POTW for permitting purposes and must supply the expanded pollutant testing list described in the EPA Application Form 2A.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of major-POTW status and the Form 2A expanded testing list could change which pollutant monitoring requirements are deemed applicable during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The EPA conducted a water quality screen which is based on the March 15, 2012 NMIP to determine if discharged pollutant concentrations demonstrate RP to exceed WQS for the various designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether pollutants were screened under this NMIP-based RP framework affects which pollutants receive enforceable limits (A) and which monitoring or limit-development obligations are triggered for screened parameters (B).

candidates.exact_span: The result of the preliminary RP analysis (see Appendix 2) indicates that Cyanide has RP to violate WQS consistent with the designated uses for the receiving waterbody.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cyanide is treated as having reasonable potential—and whether that finding is final or merely preliminary—could change whether cyanide numeric limits and related monitoring are considered applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether these cyanide values are proposed, draft, or already enforceable limits—and which statistic (daily maximum vs. monthly average) applies to a given measurement—could change compliance comparisons and the monitoring frequency implied by each limit type.
